data.gender_notes: Pratham is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘prathama’ meaning ‘first’ or ‘foremost’. In Hindu mythology, Pratham is also the name of the first celestial being or deity. It is believed that naming a child Pratham will bring them good fortune and success in their endeavors. The name Pratham carries the meaning “First” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Pratham usually hope their child will grow to embody first and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the beginning of a new journey in life.
data.etymology: Pratham belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “First.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Pratham total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Pratham carries a significant cultural impact as it is considered an auspicious name in Hindu tradition. It is believed that naming a child Pratham will bring them good fortune and success in their endeavors. It also signifies the importance of being first and setting a good example for others in one's family and community.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu mythology, the name Pratham is associated with the first celestial being or deity, signifying the beginning of all creation. It is believed that invoking the blessings of this deity will bring prosperity, happiness, and success in one's life. The name is also believed to have deep spiritual significance, as it represents the idea of being first and foremost in one's thoughts, actions, and intentions towards spiritual growth and self-realization.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Pratham means 'First' in Sanskrit. It symbolizes being the pioneer, the leader, and the one who begins a new cycle or journey. Spiritually, it also represents purity and innocence, as we are all first in the eyes of the divine.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Pratham can be found in the 'Prathama Sanhita' or the 'First Chapter' of the 'Rigveda', which is the oldest and most authoritative Hindu scripture.
historical_references.time_period: The Rigveda was composed between 1500 BCE and 1200 BCE.
